system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented global order: electoral shocks, AI race and regional wars
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is being reshaped by a confluence of political realignments, rapid technological competition, and regional military escalations. Electoral shocks in the United States have immediate spillovers for foreign policy, energy markets and tech investment, even as great‑power competition—especially over AI, chips and data‑center exposure—drives partial decoupling. Simultaneously, the Middle East and the Russia–Ukraine war continue to inject instability into energy supplies and security calculations, while cyber attacks and supply‑chain fragilities amplify systemic risk.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and major coalitions (US, China, Russia, EU, Gulf states, Iran, NATO), multinational corporations in tech and energy, global financial and commodity markets, transnational flows of data/compute, cyber and military theaters, and election-driven domestic politics that shape external policy.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic and security order (interdependent international system of states, markets, institutions and technology regimes).
adjacent_subsystems: Global technology & digital infrastructure (AI, chips, data centers)

variables.name: U.S. domestic political realignment
variables.description: A Democratic surge in U.S. midterms is rebalancing power between Congress and the presidency, reshaping oversight, fiscal levers and the U.S. stance on foreign policy, markets and tech governance.

variables.name: Iran–Gulf maritime and proxy escalation
variables.description: Iran, the United States and Gulf states are locked in an intensifying cycle of maritime attacks, strikes and proxy actions that threaten regional security and global energy supply lines.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high-intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, supported diplomatically and materially by Western partners, remain in sustained combat with shifting frontlines, strategic strikes on infrastructure and persistent implications for European security.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and trade competition
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI partnerships, investment and export controls, driving supply‑chain reconfiguration, industrial policy responses and economic decoupling pressures.

variables.name: Global AI industrialization and governance shift
variables.description: Major tech firms, investors and governments (notably in the U.S., China and EU) are racing to build AI compute, models and regulation, concentrating economic and geopolitical power while raising new market, security and governance risks.
